headline: Navier–Stokes: proof, precedence and the drawer-claim test
subtitle: A dated public theorem versus claims of much older, possibly unpublished ideas: what counts as mathematical priority?
question: How can a third party substantiate that a newly announced result was anticipated by an earlier, specific, independently checkable mathematical contribution?
intro: The September 2026 Navier–Stokes announcement illustrates the need to distinguish a proved theorem from earlier related research, a rumor or a retrospective claim. This case does not accuse any named person of misconduct.

fields.caseName: CREDEMIA 001 — Navier–Stokes priority and parallel research
fields.aTitle: Alpöge–Buckmaster: forced Euler research (separate theorem; original source pending)
fields.bTitle: On the Navier–Stokes Millennium Prize Problem
fields.comparison: Review whether any earlier, dated and accessible mathematical argument proves the same exact proposition (including Euler versus viscous Navier–Stokes, smooth forcing, domain, boundary conditions, hypotheses and blow-up conclusion). OpenAI reports distinct Euler and Navier–Stokes results. A retrospective 'I had this 10 years ago' claim is an evidentiary lead, not itself a mathematical proof or priority timestamp.

timeline.title: Clay identifies its Millennium Prize formulation
timeline.text: Official Navier–Stokes existence-and-smoothness problem established; candidate proof must match a stated alternative.

timeline.title: OpenAI says its related research began
timeline.text: A party's disclosed start date is its own account and should be contrasted with original dated technical records.

timeline.title: OpenAI reports a Navier–Stokes solution
timeline.text: Its account says the internal system produced a solution on September 5; formal verification continued.

timeline.title: OpenAI publishes its claim
timeline.text: A claimed smooth-forcing blow-up construction for the 3D Navier–Stokes system, corresponding to Clay alternatives C/D.
timeline.verification: Public dated announcement; proof not audited here

timeline.title: OpenAI adds a concurrent-work statement
timeline.text: OpenAI states Alpöge and Buckmaster had priority for a different forced-Euler result; its claim of independent development is the reporting party's account, not an independent finding by CREDEMIA.

timeline.title: Clay acknowledges apparently settled problem
timeline.text: Clay indicates the result appears to address the Millennium Problem while evaluation and assignment of credit remain deliberately unhurried.

timeline.title: Ten-years-ago notebook or code claim
timeline.text: No particular 2016 paper, notebook or exact theorem is asserted as fact by CREDEMIA. The claimant must submit an authentic dated artifact before this question can be evaluated.

reviewQuestions: What exact formal theorem is asserted in each work? Same equations, viscosity, forcing, dimensionality, initial data and conclusion?
Is the older contribution dated by an independent archive, signed commit, public preprint, publisher receipt or cryptographic timestamp?
Was the old material accessible to the later authors? Distinguish access from influence.
Does a shared mathematical theme amount to the same proof or an independent method?
Are the cited claims and counterclaims traceable to contemporaneous records?
Have both parties been offered the same source-based opportunity to correct the account?
Does any proof satisfy all of Clay's mathematical and procedural requirements? No automatic verdict.
